answers.answer: Redis is an in-memory key-value store / data structure server: a network server keeping keys mapped to typed values (strings, lists, sets, hashes, sorted sets) in RAM, with optional persistence to disk via RDB snapshots or an append only file. It is used when an on-disk database is too slow for the request path: caching (with eviction and key expiration), session stores, queues and messaging (lists, sorted sets, pub/sub, streams), and search/vectors (secondary indexing, full-text and vector similarity search; vector sets in beta). All of these are rendered as Unknown (no fidelity review).

answers.answer: The artifact names the two mechanisms: RDB snapshots, written by a forked child (rdbSaveBackground via redisFork) when serverCron finds configured save points reached; and the append only file, where feedAppendOnlyFile appends each propagated write to a memory buffer and flushAppendOnlyFile writes it to disk in beforeSleep before replies are sent. How they differ in durability: not stated (the cost rows rest on withheld redis.conf). Which is used to restore data at startup when both are enabled: not stated.

answers.answer: The event loop (ae.c, aeMain) sleeps until file descriptors are ready then processes their events. The listening socket's handler connSocketAcceptHandler (socket.c) accepts a connection and passes it to acceptCommonHandler, which creates a client; createClient installs readQueryFromClient as the read handler, which fills the query buffer and calls processInputBuffer -> processCommandAndResetClient -> processCommand -> call. Replies go into the client output buffer via addReply; beforeSleep calls handleClientsWithPendingWrites to send buffered replies and flushAppendOnlyFile to write the AOF before the loop waits again. serverCron runs periodic work such as checking save points. A complete description of one loop turn beyond this: not stated.

answers.answer: Bytes arrive; the event loop calls readQueryFromClient, which fills the query buffer and calls processInputBuffer; that chooses multibulk (input starting with *) or inline protocol, parses arguments, and calls processCommandAndResetClient once a full command is ready. processCommand looks up the command, checks ACL permissions, redirects keys owned by another cluster node, runs eviction when maxmemory is set, and refuses writes after a persistence error. Inside MULTI the command is queued and answered QUEUED; otherwise call runs the command's proc. The reply goes to the output buffer via addReply. After a write call hands it to alsoPropagate; propagateNow feeds feedAppendOnlyFile (AOF buffer, flushed to disk in beforeSleep before replies are sent) and replicationFeedSlaves (replication stream). beforeSleep sends replies with handleClientsWithPendingWrites. Other checks (e.g. what eviction failure does): not stated.

One event loop runs all commands; the stated reason is that threading is not a silver bullet and a single-threaded core keeps the design simple, with scale-out by combining many shared-nothing single-threaded instances (simpler, suits NUMA). Extra threads: optional I/O threads read, parse and write sockets; background saves use a forked child (process). Costs/conditions: maintainers suggest enabling I/O threads only on machines with at least four cores and only for a real performance problem; threaded I/O is not supported for TLS; one slow command delays every other client of the instance; repl-compression works only when io-threads is above 1.
